TYPE
   E OFF APPLICATION:          Legislative – Subdivision Plat

SYNOPSIS: Blaser Ventures proposes the Development of a 5.52-acre (240,722 sq. ft. ) vacant metes-and-
bounds Parcel at 2280 South State Street into a four-Lot mixed-use, Multi-Family Dwelling project.

The proposed Subdivision will be made up of the four Lots in the following configuration:

       Lot 1: 0.823 acres (35,866 sq. ft.)
       Lot 2: 0.570 acres (42,832 sq. ft.)
       Lot 3: 1.119 acres (48,730 sq. ft.)
       Lot 4: 2.960 acres (128,935 sq. ft.)
       TOTAL:: 5.522 acress (247,722
                                   2 sq.. ft.))

PLANNING COMMISSION AUTHORITY

       § 17.11.030 Land use authority designations.

Pursuant to state law, the following administrative land use authority designations are made:

       A. Planning Commission. The planning commission is the land use authority on issues of:
          subdivision and subdivision plat approval, vacating, altering or amending a Subdivision Plat;
          Conditional Use Permit Applications; design review for Building Heights as established in this
          Title; design review for projects on Parcels where any portion of the Parcel abuts any residential
          district; and the issuance of a Building or demolition permit in a Historic and Landmark district.

GENERAL PLAN CONSIDERATIONS

       Land Use & Neighborhoods Goal 1.
                   Continue to welcome new residents and businesses into South Salt Lake.

       Analysis:      The proposed Development will add 478 new residential units in the city, with at
                      least 400 units dedicated to affordable housing.

       Land Use & Neighborhoods Goal 3.
                   Enhance urban and streetscape design in the city to support South Salt Lake’s
                   distinct image and enhance community pride.



                                                     7
      Analysis:     The proposed Development will improve the streetscape along Main Street, Central
                    Pointe Place, State Street, and Haven Avenue.

      Housing Goal 2.
                   Connect housing of various densities to appropriate services and amenities within
                   and between neighborhoods.

      Analysis:     The Applicant proposes including commercial space on Lots 2, 3, and 4 of the
                    Market Center Subdivision. This commercial space will provide additional services
                    and amenities for residents in and around the Development.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION

Based upon the information submitted in the application, supporting documentation, and analysis of the
relevant code sections and general plan goals, Staff recommends the Planning Commission move to
approve the Market Center Preliminary Subdivision Plat to create four Lots located at 2280 South State
Street, based on the Findings of Fact, Conclusions of Law, and Conditions of Approval for the Millcreek
Station Subdivision in the staff report.

FINDINGS OF FACT:

   1. The property is located at 2280 South State Street in the Downtown District, Station Subdistrict.

   2. The parcel number is 16-19-151-013-0000.

   3. The parcel contains 5.52 acres (247,722 sq. ft.).

   4. The property is currently vacant.

   5. The purpose of the proposed Subdivision is to create four Lots to construct four distinct buildings
      for a mixed-use, Multi-Family Development.

   6. The addresses for each Lot are:
         a. Lot 1: 2263 South Main Street
         b. Lot 2: 54 East Central Pointe Place
         c. Lot 3: 2280 South State Street
         d. Lot 4: 53 East Haven Avenue

   7. The proposed Lot sizes are:
         a. Lot 1: 0.823 acres (35,866 sq. ft.)
         b. Lot 2: 0.570 acres (42,832 sq. ft.)

                                                    11
          c. Lot 3: 1.119 acres (48,730 sq. ft.)
          d. Lot 4: 2.960 acres (128,935 sq. ft.)

   8. There is no environmentally sensitive land on site and no impact is expected on environmentally
      sensitive lands.

   9. Multi-Family Dwelling is a Conditional Use in the Downtown District.

   10. The proposed Subdivision will comply with all requirements of the South Salt Lake Municipal Code.

   11. Staff reviewed this Subdivision application for compliance with South Salt Lake Municipal Code
       Sections 17.10.120, 17.10.130, 17.10.140, 17.10.150, 17.10.160, 17.10.170, 17.10.180, 17.10.190
       and 17.10.200, and found that this subdivision application is compliant with this section, as outlined
       above.

   Conclusions of Law:

   1. The use, as specifically conditioned below, is consistent with the South Salt Lake City General Plan.

   2. The use, as specifically conditioned below, is compatible in use, scale, and design with allowed
      uses in the Downtown District.

   3. The use, as specifically conditioned below, does not compromise the health, safety, or welfare of:
      Persons employed within or using the proposed Development; Those residing or working in the
      vicinity of the proposed use or Development; or Property or improvements in the vicinity of the
      proposed use or Development.

   4. The use, as specifically conditioned below, does not impose disproportionate burdens on the
      citizens of South Salt Lake.

Conditions of Approval:

   1. The Applicant shall continue working with city staff to make all necessary technical corrections
      before recording.

   2. Prior to plat recordation and any additional Development of the subsequent Lots, the Applicant
      must provide city staff the final plat mylar with notarized signatures of owners’ consent to
      dedication; obtain signatures of all entities indicated on the subdivision plat attached hereto.

   3. The plat shall indicate a 5-foot public utility easement along the front Lot lines of each Lot pursuant
      to South Salt Lake Municipal Code § 17.10.190(B)(2).

   4. The Applicant shall complete (or post an adequate improvement completion assurance), warrant
      and post required warranty assurance for all public infrastructure improvements including
      streetlights.

   5. The Applicant shall ensure that all site improvements are installed consistent with the requirements
      of the South Salt Lake City Municipal Code.

   6. The proposed Development shall meet all requirements of the South Salt Lake City Municipal
      Code, unless specifically exempted through a fully executed Development Agreement.



                                                     12
   7. The proposed Development shall meet all requirements of the South Salt Lake Community
      Development Department, South Salt Lake Fire Marshal, the South Salt Lake Building Official, and
      the South Salt Lake Engineering Department.

   8. The Applicant shall comply with all applicable International Building Codes and International Fire
      Codes and must obtain and complete a South Salt Lake building permit.

   9. The Applicant shall record the plat with the Salt Lake County Recorder’s Office prior to ratification
      of a Development Agreement. Otherwise, the Applicant shall record the plat within two years of
      receiving final plat approval.

   10. All items of the staff report.

PLANNING COMMISSION OPTIONS

Option 1: Approval
Move to approve the application by Blaser Ventures for a Preliminary Subdivision Plat to create four Lots
located at 2280 South State Street, based on the Findings of Fact, Conclusions of Law, and Conditions of
Approval in the staff report and enumerated on the record.

Option 2: Denial
Move to deny the application by Blaser Ventures for a Preliminary Subdivision Plat to create four Lots located
at 2280 South State Street, based on the Findings of Fact, Conclusions of Law, and Conditions of Approval
in the staff report and enumerated on the record.

Option 3: Continuance
Move to table the application by Blaser Ventures for a Preliminary Subdivision Plat to create four Lots located
at 2280 South State Street to a date certain to allow the Applicants and Staff time to respond to specific
inquiries or concerns raised by the Planning Commission, or to allow the Planning Commission more time to
consider the proposal.

                               PLANNING COMMISSION STAFF REPORT
MEETING DATE:                 April 17, 2025
PROJECT NUMBER:               S24-00024
REQUEST(S):                   An application for a Preliminary Subdivision Plat to amend an existing subdivision
                              plat located at 3535 South State Street.
ADDRESS:                      3535 South State Street and 140 E Winslow Avenue
PARCEL NUMBERS:               16-31-103-024 and 16-31-103-003-0000
PROPERTY OWNER:                       Katmark Partners, LLC
APPLICANT:                    Mark Miller Subaru
TYPE OF APPLICATION:          Administrate – Subdivision Plat

SYNOPSIS:
On November 18, 2024, Mark Miller Subaru
submitted a plat application to amend the existing
plat. The plat application is to consolidate two
properties into one lot, in order to expand the
existing Auto Dealership, Mark Miller Subaru.

As part of this, Mark Miller Subaru will also need to
amend their Conditional Use Permit (CUP) since
they are expanding their dealership operations.

The subject property located at 140 East Winslow
Avenue is currently vacant land. It will be paved for
parking for their inventory. As part of the project,
the applicant will be required to install a 10-foot
landscape buffer along the east portion of the
property, since they are adjacent to a single-family
residential home. They have already installed an 8-foot solid fence, which is required per code for buffering.
Mark Miller Subaru will also be installing a sidewalk and park strip along Winslow Avenue along their entire
property line on Winslow Avenue.

The subject property at 3535 South State Street is the existing Subaru Dealership. There will be no changes
to any of the existing dealership.

The Planning Commission is the land use authority for a subdivision plat approvals.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION:
Staff recommends the Planning Commission approve the preliminary subdivision plat to amend an existing
subdivision plat located at 3535 South State Street. Staff’s recommendation is based upon its analysis and
findings included below.

PLANNING COMMISSION AUTHORITY:
17.11.030. Land use authority designations.
Pursuant to state law, the following administrative land use authority designations are made:

   A. Planning Commission. The planning commission is the land use authority on issues of: Subdivision and
      Subdivision Plat approval, vacating, altering or amending a Subdivision Plat; Conditional Use Permit
      Applications; design review for Building Heights as established in this Title; design review for projects
      on Parcels where any portion of the Parcel abuts any residential district; and the issuance of a Building
      or demolition permit in a Historic and Landmark district.


GENERAL PLAN CONSIDERATIONS:

Economic Development Vision Statement: South Salt Lake is a community of opportunity for a variety of
businesses with diverse ownership serving a diverse community. Quality of life in South Salt Lake is enhanced
through sustainable businesses in a sustainable community. South Salt Lake encourages and supports
businesses by helping them form, expand, and thrive in our community. We build on past success for our future.

       Analysis: The Economic Development Vision Statement calls out encouraging and supporting
       businesses to expand and thrive in the community. As stated above Mark Miller Subaru has been at this
       location in the City since 1961. They purchased 140 E Winslow Avenue in early 2021. This consolidation
       will allow a long existing, sustainable business, to expand its operations and continue to thrive in the
       City.

Economic Development Strategy 5: Maintain and enhance neighborhood health, vitality, and integrity.

       Analysis: One of the actions for this strategy is “encourage incremental development where appropriate
       to avoid vacant and underutilized parcels”. The property at 140 E Winslow Avenue is vacant and no
       development or building permits can be issued until a subdivision plat has been completed and
       recorded. Additionally, a sidewalk and park strip will be installed along the Mark Miller property on
       Winslow Avenue. Currently there is no sidewalk, curb, gutter, or park strip on the south side of Winslow
       Avenue.

 STAFF RECOMMENDATION:
Staff recommends the Planning Commission approve the preliminary subdivision plat to consolidate two
properties into one-lot, located at 3535 South State Street, based upon the information submitted by the
applicant, the general plan considerations and ordinance analysis and proposes the following Findings of Fact,
Conclusions of Law and Conditions of Approval.

Findings of Fact:

    1. On November 18, 2024, Mark Miller Subaru submitted a plat application to consolidate two properties,
       in order to expand the existing Auto Dealership.

    2. The subject parcels are located at 3535 South State Street and 140 East Winslow Avenue.

    3. The two properties are located in the Commercial Corridor land use district.

    4. The proposed consolidation plat will be a total of 7.53-acre lot.

    5. The business will have access from State Street, Winslow Avenue, Baird Avenue, and 200 East.

Conclusions of Law:

    1.   The use, as specifically conditioned below, is consistent with the South Salt Lake City General Plan.

    2.   The use, as specifically conditioned below, is compatible in use, scale, and design with allowed uses
         in the Commercial Corridor land use district.

    3.   The subdivision as specifically conditioned below, does not compromise the health, safety, or welfare
         of: Persons employed within or using the proposed development; Those residing or working in the
         vicinity of the proposed use or development; or Property or improvements in the vicinity of the
         proposed use or development.

    4.   The subdivision, as specifically conditioned below does not impose disproportionate burdens on the
         citizens of the city.

    5.   Staff has reviewed this subdivision for compliance with SSL Municipal Code Section “17.10.140
         Subdivision Development Lot Standards” and found that this subdivision is compliant with this
         section, as outlined above.

    6.   Staff has reviewed this subdivision for compliance with SSL Municipal Code Section “17.10.150
         Subdivision and Condominium Plat Layout Requirements” and found that this subdivision is compliant
         with this section, as outlined above.

    7.   Staff has reviewed this subdivision for compliance with SSL Municipal Code Sections 17.10.160,
         17.10.170, 17.10.180, 17.10.190, 17.10.200, and 17.10.210, and found that this subdivision is
         compliant with those sections, as outlined above.

Conditions of Approval:

    1. The applicant will continue to work with City staff to make all technical corrections necessary prior to
       recording;



                                                      9
     2. Prior to plat recordation and issuance of full building permits for the subsequent lot, the applicant must
        provide city staff the final plat mylar to include notarized signatures of owners’ consent to dedication;
        obtain signatures of all entities indicated on the subdivision plat attached hereto;

     3. The applicant shall complete (or post an adequate improvement completion assurance), warrant and
        post required warranty assurance for all required landscaping and public infrastructure improvements
        including street lights, within two years of receiving final plat approval;

     4. The applicant shall ensure that all site improvements are installed consistent with the requirements of
        the South Salt Lake City Municipal Code;

     5. The applicant shall dedicate an easement to the City of South Salt Lake for purposes of storm water
        management practices and ensure the plat includes language of the dedication of such easement, in
        a form as approved by the City Attorney’s Office;

     6. The proposed development shall meet all requirements of the South Salt Lake Community
        Development Department, South Salt Lake Fire Marshal, the South Salt Lake Building Official, and the
        South Salt Lake Engineering department;

     7. The applicant shall comply with all applicable International Building Codes and International Fire
        Codes and must obtain and complete a South Salt Lake building permit;

     8. The applicant shall record the plat with the Salt Lake County Recorder’s Office within 365 days of
        receiving final plat approval; or the approval will expire. However, if the applicant elects to install
        Infrastructure Improvements has deposited a 10% Warranty Assurance, and is actively working on the
        issued building permit, the plat approval will not expire until two years after final plat approval.

     9. All undergrounding of utilities shall be completed within 365 days of receiving final plat approval; and

     10. All items of the staff report.

 PLANNING COMMISSION OPTIONS:
Option 1: Approval
Move to approve an application by Mark Miller Subaru to consolidate two properties into one-lot located at
3535 South State Street, based on the Findings of Fact, Conclusions of Law, and Conditions of Approval as
outlined in the staff report and enumerated on the record.

Option 2: Denial
Move to deny the application by Mark Miller Subaru to consolidate two properties into one-lot located at 3535
South State Street, based on the findings discussed on the record.

Option 3: Continuance
Move to table the decision on the application by Mark Miller Subaru to consolidate two properties into one-lot
located at 3535 South State Street, to a date certain to allow the Applicant and Staff time to respond to specific
inquires or concerns raised by the Planning Commission, or to allow the Planning Commission more time to
consider the proposal.

                              PLANNING COMMISSION STAFF REPORT
MEETING DATE:                April 17, 2025
PROJECT NUMBER:              C25-00003
REQUEST:                     An application to amend an existing Conditional Use Permit C-19-013, for an Auto
                             Dealership, located at 3535 South State Street.
ADDRESS:                     3535 South State Street and 140 E Winslow Avenue
PARCEL NUMBERS:              16-31-103-024 and 16-31-103-003-0000
PROPERTY OWNER:              Katmark Partners, LLC
APPLICANT:                   Mark Miller Subaru
TYPE OF APPLICATION:         Administrative – Conditional Use Permit
SYNOPSIS:
On November 18, 2024, Mark Miller Subaru
submitted a Conditional Use Permit (“CUP”)
application, to expand their existing an Auto
Dealership from 3535 South to 140 E Winslow
Avenue.

The CUP is required as part of expansion of the site
which is being done via a plat. Mark Miller Subaru
is the existing dealership at this location. At this
time, the only change is an expansion of the
parking lot. The proposed expansion is 0.18 acres
along Winslow Avenue, which will add 18 more
parking stalls. Currently, this parcel, 140 E Winslow
Avenue is vacant. As part of the project, the
applicant will be required to install a 10-foot
landscape buffer along the east portion of the property, since they are adjacent to a single-family residential
home. They have already installed an 8-foot solid fence, which is required per code for buffering. Mark Miller
Subaru will also be installing a sidewalk and park strip along Winslow Avenue along their entire property line
on Winslow Avenue.

The Planning Commission is the land use authority over all Conditional Use Permits.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION:
Staff recommends the Planning Commission approve a Conditional Use Permit, to amend the existing CUP,
C-19-013, to include the property located at 140 E Winslow Avenue. Staff’s recommendation is based upon
its analysis and findings included below.

PLANNING COMMISSION AUTHORITY:


17.11.030. Land use authority designations.

Pursuant to state law, the following administrative land use authority designations are made:

   A. Planning Commission. The planning commission is the land use authority on issues of: subdivision
      and subdivision plat approval, vacating, altering, or amending a Subdivision Plat; Conditional Use
      Permit Applications; design review for Building Heights as established in this Title; design review for
      projects on Parcels where any portion of the Parcel abuts any residential district; and the issuance of a
      Building or demolition permit in a Historic and Landmark district.

CONDITIONAL USE REVIEW STANDARD:
Utah Code Ann. § 10-9a-507(2) sets forth the following standard of review for conditional uses by stating:

    (a)     (i)       A land use authority shall approve a conditional use if reasonable conditions are proposed,
                      or can be imposed, to mitigate the reasonably anticipated detrimental effects of the
                      proposed use in accordance with applicable standards.
            (ii)       The requirement described in Subsection (2)(a)(i) to reasonably mitigate anticipated
                       detrimental effects of the proposed conditional use does not require elimination of the
                       detrimental effects.
    (b)            If a land use authority proposes reasonable conditions on a proposed conditional use, the land
                   use authority shall ensure that the conditions are stated on the record and reasonably relate to
                   mitigating the anticipated detrimental effects of the proposed use.
    (c)     If the reasonably anticipated detrimental effects of a proposed conditional use cannot be
            substantially mitigated by the proposal or the imposition of reasonable conditions to achieve
            compliance with applicable standards, the land use authority may deny the conditional use.

South Salt Lake Municipal Code §17.05 sets forth the following standard for review for conditional uses by
stating:

                                                          4
   A. A person seeking approval of a Conditional Use must file a Complete Application, using the forms
      established by the Community Development Department, and include payment of all fees. For any
      Application to construct a Building or other improvement to property for a Use that is defined by this
      Code as allowed in the zoning district in which the Building is proposed, the Community Development
      Department and the City Engineer must review the Application to determine whether the proposal:
          1. Is allowed within the district where it is proposed;
          2. Is proposed for Development on a legally subdivided Lot;
          3. Can be adequately serviced by Dedicated roads, improved to City Standards and existing or
              proposed utility systems or lines;
          4. Complies with all applicable Development requirements of that district, including Building
              Height, Setbacks, and Lot Coverage;
          5. Meets the applicable Development Standards requirements;
          6. Conforms to the Design Guidelines and the design review process established for that district;
          7. Requires additional conditions of approval;
          8. Complies with the Construction Codes; and
          9. Pertains to land for which all tax assessments have been paid
   B. The Community Development Department staff shall notify the Applicant of any specific deficiencies in
      the proposal.
   C. No permit or license issued shall be valid if any of the criteria listed in this Section have not been met.

 GENERAL PLAN CONSIDERATIONS:

 Economic Development Vision Statement: South Salt Lake is a community of opportunity for a variety of
businesses with diverse ownership serving a diverse community. Quality of life in South Salt Lake is enhanced
through sustainable businesses in a sustainable community. South Salt Lake encourages and supports
businesses by helping them form, expand, and thrive in our community. We build on past success for our
future.
        Analysis: The Economic Development Vision Statement calls out encouraging and supporting
        businesses to expand and thrive in the community. As stated above Mark Miller Subaru has been at this
        location in the City since 1961. They purchased 140 E Winslow Avenue in early 2021. The CUP would
        allow a long existing, sustainable business, to expand its operations and continue to thrive in the City.

Economic Development Strategy 5: Maintain and enhance neighborhood health, vitality, and integrity.

       Analysis: The CUP process will put conditions in place that will mitigate any potential impacts from the
       use. The CUP will ensure that the surrounding neighborhood health, vitality, and integrity, is not
       impacted by the business. Additionally, a sidewalk and park strip will be installed along the Mark Miller
       property on Winslow Avenue. Currently there is no sidewalk, curb, gutter, or park strip on the south side
       of Winslow Avenue.

  STAFF RECOMMENDATION:
Staff recommends the Planning Commission approve a Conditional Use Permit C25-00003, for Mark Miller
Subaru, an Auto Dealership, located at 3535 South State Street, with the following conditions:

Findings of Fact:

     1.   On November 18, 2024, Mark Miller Subaru, submitted a Conditional Use Permit application, in order
          to amend an existing CUP, C-19-013 for the Auto Dealership, located at 3535 South State Street.

     2.   The subject property is located at 3535 South State Street and 140 East Winslow Avenue.

     3.   The new property they are adding is 0.18 acres. This is less than 10% of the entire site.

     4.   The applicant applied for a subdivision application on November 17, 2024, to consolidate the
          subject properties by plat to comply with South Salt Lake Municipal Code.

     5.   The site is approximately 7.53 acres.

     6.   The two properties are located in the Commercial Corridor land use district.

     7.   The business will have access from State Street, Winslow Avenue, Baird Avenue, and 200 East.

     8.   The photometric study does not have any light trespass measured at 0.5 foot-candles at 5’ at the
          property line.

                                                       12
     9.    Section 17.03.010 of the City Code classifies Auto, Light Truck, RV, Boat, Trailer Dealerships (Sale,
           Lease, or Rent) as Conditional Uses subject to Planning Commission approval.

Conclusions of Law:

    1.    The use, as specifically conditioned below, is consistent with the South Salt Lake City General Plan.

    2.    The use, as specifically conditioned below, is compatible in use, scale, and design with allowed uses
          in the Commercial Corridor land use district.

    3.    The use, as specifically conditioned below, does not compromise the health, safety, or welfare of:
          Persons employed within or using the proposed development; Those residing or working in the
          vicinity of the proposed use or development; or Property or improvements in the vicinity of the
          proposed use or development.

    4.    As there are no environmentally sensitive lands on site, no impact to environmentally sensitive lands
          is expected to occur as part of the business.

    5.    The use, as specifically conditioned below does not impose disproportionate burdens on the citizens
          of the city.

    6.    The use, as specifically conditioned below, meets the standards found in Section 17.05.010,
          17.05.020, 17.05.030, 17.05.040, 17.05.050, and 17.05.060, as outlined above.

    7.    No specific hazards or adverse impacts are expected due to the proposed use.

    8.    This is not considered an expansion of a Conditional Use because the subject property is not being
          expanded by greater than 10 percent of existing square footage, as outlined in 17.05.080.

    9.    The photometric study is compliant with the standards listed in 17.06.140(C)(5).

Conditions of Approval:

    1.    The applicant shall comply will all Conditions of Approval from C-19-013;

    2.    The applicant shall maintain the 10-foot fencing where the new portion of the dealership lot abuts the
          Single-Family Use;

    3.    The applicant shall maintain the landscape buffers where the new portion of the dealership lot abuts
          the Single-Family Use;

    4.    Under no circumstances are deliveries to be conducted after 10:00PM;

    5.    All items of the staff report.

 PLANNING COMMISSION OPTIONS:
 Option 1: Approval
 Move to approve the application submitted for a Conditional Use Permit, C25-00003, to amend an existing
 CUP, C-19-0013, for the existing Auto Dealership, located at 3535 South State Street, based on the Findings
 of Fact, Conclusions of Law, and Conditions of Approval as outlined in the staff report and enumerated on
 the record.


                                                       13
Option 2: Denial
Move to deny the application submitted for a Conditional Use Permit, C25-00003, to amend an existing CUP,
C-19-0013, for the existing Auto Dealership, located at 3535 South State Street, based on the reasoning set
forth in the record.

Option 3: Continuance
Move to table the decision on the application submitted for a Conditional Use Permit, C25-00003, to amend
an existing CUP, C-19-0013, for the existing Auto Dealership, located at 3535 South State Street, to a date
certain to allow the Applicant and Staff time to respond to specific inquiries or concerns raised by the Planning
Commission, or to allow the Planning Commission more time to consider the proposal.

Fee Title Owner: Katmark Partners, LLC

Date: April 17, 2025

Permit Issued to:      Katmark Partners, LLC
                       3535 South State Street
                       SSL, Utah 84115

Findings of Fact:

   1.   On November 18, 2024, Mark Miller Subaru, submitted a Conditional Use Permit
        application, in order to amend an existing CUP, C-19-013 for the Auto Dealership,
        located at 3535 South State Street.

   2.   The subject property is located at 3535 South State Street and 140 East Winslow
        Avenue.

   3.   The new property they are adding is 0.18 acres. This is less than 10% of the entire site.

   4.   The applicant applied for a subdivision application on November 17, 2024, to
        consolidate the subject properties by plat to comply with South Salt Lake Municipal
        Code.

   5.   The site is approximately 7.53 acres.

   6.   The two properties are located in the Commercial Corridor land use district.

   7.   The business will have access from State Street, Winslow Avenue, Baird Avenue, and
        200 East.

   8.   The photometric study does not have any light trespass measured at 0.5 foot-candles
        at 5’ at the property line.




                                                  1
   9.   Section 17.03.010 of the City Code classifies Auto, Light Truck, RV, Boat, Trailer
        Dealerships (Sale, Lease, or Rent) as Conditional Uses subject to Planning Commission
        approval.

   10. On June 25, 2021, Katmark Partners, LLC, submitted a Conditional Use Permit
       application, in order to expand the existing Auto Dealership on site.

   11. The subject property is located at 3535 South State Street, 130 East Winslow Avenue,
       and 3549-3555 South 200 East.

   12. The applicant applied for a subdivision application on June 25, 2021, to consolidate
       the subject properties by plat to comply with South Salt Lake Municipal Code. The
       preliminary subdivision plat was approved by the Planning Commission on January
       18, 2024;

   13. The site is approximately 7.19 acres.

   14. All three parcels are located in the Commercial Corridor land use district.

   15. The business will have access from State Street, Winslow Avenue, Baird Avenue, and
       200 East.

   16. The photometric study is compliant with the standards listed in 17.06.140(C)(5).

   17. Section 17.03.010 of the City Code classifies Auto, Light Truck, RV, Boat, Trailer
       Dealerships (Sale, Lease, or Rent) as Conditional Uses subject to Planning Commission
       approval.

Conclusions of Law:

   1.   The use, as specifically conditioned below, is consistent with the South Salt Lake City
        General Plan.

   2.   The use, as specifically conditioned below, is compatible in use, scale, and design with
        allowed uses in the Commercial Corridor land use district.

   3.   The use, as specifically conditioned below, does not compromise the health, safety, or
        welfare of: Persons employed within or using the proposed development; Those
        residing or working in the vicinity of the proposed use or development; or Property or
        improvements in the vicinity of the proposed use or development.

   4.   As there are no environmentally sensitive lands on site, no impact to environmentally
        sensitive lands is expected to occur as part of the business.

   5.   The use, as specifically conditioned below does not impose disproportionate burdens
        on the citizens of the city.




                                               2
   6.   The use, as specifically conditioned below, meets the standards found in Section
        17.05.010, 17.05.020, 17.05.030, 17.05.040, 17.05.050, and 17.05.060, as outlined
        above.

   7.   No specific hazards or adverse impacts are expected due to the proposed use.

   8.   This is not considered an expansion of a Conditional Use because the subject property
        is not being expanded by greater than 10 percent of existing square footage, as
        outlined in 17.05.080.

   9.   The photometric study is compliant with the standards listed in 17.06.140(C)(5).

Conditions of Approval:

   1.   The applicant shall comply will all Conditions of Approval from C-19-013;

   2.   The applicant shall maintain the 10-foot fencing where the new portion of the
        dealership lot abuts the Single-Family Use;

   3.   The applicant shall maintain the landscape buffers where the new portion of the
        dealership lot abuts the Single-Family Use;

   4.   Under no circumstances are deliveries to be conducted after 10:00PM;

   5.   The applicant shall comply with all of the conditions of approval below and within the
        Conditional Use Permit prior to the release of a South Salt Lake building permit;

   6.   The Auto Dealership shall meet all requirements of the South Salt Lake Community
        Development Department, South Salt Lake Fire Marshal, the South Salt Lake Building
        Official, and the South Salt Lake Engineering department;

   7.   The applicant shall comply with all federal, state, and local laws, including the
        development standards.

   8.   The applicant shall maintain a minimum of 15 vehicle display stalls and a minimum of
        three (3) employee parking stalls on-site;

   9.   The applicant shall maintain the 8-foot fencing where the dealership is expanding;

   10. The applicant shall maintain the landscape buffers where the dealership is expanding;

   11. Any new expansion or realignment of the parking lot, shall require the business to meet
       the landscaping and fencing standards at the time;

   12. The applicant shall remove any trash and solid waste that builds up on the property;

   13. The applicant shall not use the panic button to find cars on the lot;




                                              3
   14. Outside speakers, lighting, deliveries, and other maintenance such as emptying of
       waste containers shall not occur before 7:00AM or after 10:00PM. There may be a
       security light left on after 10:00PM for CPTED purposes;

   15. Any expansion or new construction to the building or site in the future would require a
       design review approval from the Planning Commission;

   16. Double stacking of cars in the display lot is prohibited;

   17. All cars on the lot shall meet all requirements of the law at all times, shall be in operating
       condition, shall not have flat tires or broken windows, and shall be capable of being
       licensed and registered without additional repair or alteration;

   18. The display lot as outlined in the site plan may not be reduced;

   19. The western curb cut along Winslow Avenue will need to be closed off. The remaining
       curb cut shall be a minimum of 100 feet from State Street.

   20. The maximum illumination, when measured at the Property Line at a height of five feet
       and facing the light fixture(s), shall be no greater than 0.5 foot-candles; and

   21. All items of the staff report.

Dear South Salt Lake Planning Commission,

We appreciate the opportunity to update you on the steps we have taken to ensure we remain a
positive and responsible corporate neighbor. We take community concerns seriously and have
implemented several improvements to address them:

   ●​ Lighting Adjustments: We have modified our pole lights to minimize impact on
      surrounding properties and ensure they remain off throughout the night. Our lighting
      schedule currently exceeds the code requirements of turning off by 10 PM as we have all
      our main lot lights set to turn off by 9:30.
   ●​ Noise Reduction Measures:
          ○​ We invested in trash and recycling compactors, significantly reducing noise
              concerns. This improvement has also decreased trash pickups to only once
              every 5-6 weeks.
          ○​ Our new digital price tag system is fully operational and making a significant
              impact in the quiet locating of cars. We haven’t received any noise-related
              concerns since this update.
   ●​ Safety Enhancements: We have closed a lot entrance on Winslow Ave, to improve
      safety for both drivers and pedestrians.
   ●​ Community Integration: To support neighborhood cohesion and growth, we have
      placed a previously owned residential property back on the market. We are pleased to
      share that the home is now under contract.
   ●​ Buffer Improvements: An 8-foot tall Trex fence has been installed to create a strong
      and lasting buffer between our property and the neighborhood. As our lot and facility
      improvements continue we are looking at additional ways to create buffers through
      landscaping.

We are committed to maintaining a positive relationship with the community and will continue to
listen and adapt to ensure we meet the highest standards as a corporate neighbor.
